\chapter{Letters From Food, Noon and Going}
\label{ch:ar-letters-from-food-noon-going}
\hlchaptermodality{49}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can write ta, za and dhal, and I have now written every letter the words of this book use.}

Complete the last lesson of chapter 49: i can write ta, za and dhal, and I have now written every letter the words of this book use.

\section[ṭāʾ]{\ar{ط} (ṭāʾ) — the letter that opens \ar{طعام}}

\label{lesson:AR-W49-ta-emphatic}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: write \ar{ز} and \ar{غ} once each, and name them.

Now say \textbf{\ar{طعام}} (\emph{ṭaʿām}), \textquotedblleft{}food\textquotedblright{}. You have read it for a long time. This lesson takes one letter out of it and puts it in your hand.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Script you'll notice: \ar{ط}}
\textbf{\ar{ط}} — \emph{ṭāʾ}, a heavy \emph{t}.

It opens \textbf{\ar{طعام}} (\emph{ṭaʿām}), \textquotedblleft{}food\textquotedblright{}. A closed \textbf{oval} on the line, and a \textbf{tall upright} drawn last, from the top down.

\subsection*{Writing: \ar{ط}}
\hlblockfigure{\detokenize{figures/AR-W49-ta-emphatic-filmstrip.pdf}}{How \ar{ط} is written, stroke by stroke}

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \textbf{1.} start here: loop counterclockwise around the closed oval
  \item \textbf{2.} finish left along the baseline without lifting
  \item \textbf{3.} lift once, then draw the tall upright top-to-bottom — and only now lift
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Pen lifts: 1.}

\begin{quote}
Stroke order is one attested teaching order; hands and teachers vary. Source: Introduction to Arabic: Egyptian Arabic for first-year students, Alphabet \ar{ط} \ar{ظ}, independent emphatic Taa at 00:01.2–00:03.0 (University of Oregon Libraries Open Textbook, 2023; accessed 2026-08-23).
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Look:} at \textbf{\ar{طعام}} and point at \ar{ط} inside it
  \item \emph{Trace it:} \ar{ط} three times, saying \emph{ṭ} as you finish each one
  \item \emph{Write it:} \ar{غ}, then \ar{ط}, from memory
  \item \emph{Read it:} \textbf{\ar{طعام}} aloud once more
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Which letter is this — \ar{ط}? (\textbf{ṭāʾ}, \emph{ṭ}.) Which word did it come from? (\textbf{\ar{طعام}}, \emph{ṭaʿām}, \textquotedblleft{}food\textquotedblright{}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[ẓāʾ]{\ar{ظ} (ẓāʾ) — the letter inside \ar{الظهر}}

\label{lesson:AR-W49-za-emphatic}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: write \ar{غ} and \ar{ط} once each, and name them.

Now say \textbf{\ar{الظهر}} (\emph{aẓ-ẓuhr}), \textquotedblleft{}noon\textquotedblright{}. You have read it for a long time. This lesson takes one letter out of it and puts it in your hand.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Script you'll notice: \ar{ظ}}
\textbf{\ar{ظ}} — \emph{ẓāʾ}, a heavy \emph{dh}.

It is inside \textbf{\ar{الظهر}} (\emph{aẓ-ẓuhr}), \textquotedblleft{}noon\textquotedblright{}. It is \textbf{\ar{ط}}, from the last lesson, with \textbf{one dot above}.

\subsection*{Writing: \ar{ظ}}
\hlblockfigure{\detokenize{figures/AR-W49-za-emphatic-filmstrip.pdf}}{How \ar{ظ} is written, stroke by stroke}

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \textbf{1.} start here: loop counterclockwise around the closed oval
  \item \textbf{2.} finish left along the baseline without lifting
  \item \textbf{3.} lift once, then place the upper dot
  \item \textbf{4.} lift again, then draw the tall upright top-to-bottom — and only now lift
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Pen lifts: 2.}

\begin{quote}
Stroke order is one attested teaching order; hands and teachers vary. Source: Introduction to Arabic: Egyptian Arabic for first-year students, Alphabet \ar{ط} \ar{ظ}, independent emphatic DHaa at 00:01.3–00:02.8 (University of Oregon Libraries Open Textbook, 2023; accessed 2026-08-23).
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Look:} at \textbf{\ar{الظهر}} and point at \ar{ظ} inside it
  \item \emph{Trace it:} \ar{ظ} three times, saying \emph{ẓ} as you finish each one
  \item \emph{Write it:} \ar{ط}, then \ar{ظ}, from memory
  \item \emph{Read it:} \textbf{\ar{الظهر}} aloud once more
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Which letter is this — \ar{ظ}? (\textbf{ẓāʾ}, \emph{ẓ}.) Which word did it come from? (\textbf{\ar{الظهر}}, \emph{aẓ-ẓuhr}, \textquotedblleft{}noon\textquotedblright{}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[dhāl]{\ar{ذ} (dhāl) — the letter that opens \ar{ذهب}}

\label{lesson:AR-W49-dhal}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: write \ar{ط} and \ar{ظ} once each, and name them.

Now say \textbf{\ar{ذهب}} (\emph{dhahaba}), \textquotedblleft{}he went\textquotedblright{}. You have read it for a long time. This lesson takes one letter out of it and puts it in your hand.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Script you'll notice: \ar{ذ}}
\textbf{\ar{ذ}} — \emph{dhāl}, the \emph{th} of English \textquotedblleft{}this\textquotedblright{}.

It opens \textbf{\ar{ذهب}} (\emph{dhahaba}), \textquotedblleft{}he went\textquotedblright{}, the first verb in this book. It is \textbf{\ar{د}} (\emph{dāl}) with \textbf{one dot above}, and like \textbf{\ar{د}} it never joins to the letter after it.

\subsection*{Writing: \ar{ذ}}
\hlblockfigure{\detokenize{figures/AR-W49-dhal-filmstrip.pdf}}{How \ar{ذ} is written, stroke by stroke}

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \textbf{1.} start here: begin at the upper tip and descend diagonally down and right through the curved shoulder
  \item \textbf{2.} turn left along the baseline without lifting
  \item \textbf{3.} lift once, then place the dot above — and only now lift
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Pen lifts: 1.}

\begin{quote}
Stroke order is one attested teaching order; hands and teachers vary. Source: Introduction to Arabic: Egyptian Arabic for first-year students, Alphabet: \ar{د} \ar{ذ} \ar{ر}, independent Dhaal body followed by its upper dot (University of Oregon Libraries Open Textbook, 2023; accessed 2026-08-21).
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Look:} at \textbf{\ar{ذهب}} and point at \ar{ذ} inside it
  \item \emph{Trace it:} \ar{ذ} three times, saying \emph{dh} as you finish each one
  \item \emph{Write it:} \ar{ظ}, then \ar{ذ}, from memory
  \item \emph{Read it:} \textbf{\ar{ذهب}} aloud once more
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Which letter is this — \ar{ذ}? (\textbf{dhāl}, \emph{dh}.) Which word did it come from? (\textbf{\ar{ذهب}}, \emph{dhahaba}, \textquotedblleft{}he went\textquotedblright{}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[arbaʿat ʿashar ḥarfan]{(fourteen letters) — Fourteen letters, fourteen words — a first pass}

\label{lesson:AR-R49-letters-first-pass}



\begin{quote}
Write the letter that opens \ar{شكرا}, then the one that opens \ar{صباح}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\noindent
\begin{tabularx}{\linewidth}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{letter} & \textbf{name} & \textbf{the word it came from} \\
\midrule
\ar{ش} & \emph{shīn} & \textbf{\ar{شكرا}} \emph{shukran} \\
\ar{ص} & \emph{ṣād} & \textbf{\ar{صباح} \ar{الخير}} \emph{ṣabāḥ al-khayr} \\
\ar{د} & \emph{dāl} & \textbf{\ar{الحمد} \ar{لله}} \emph{al-ḥamdu lillāh} \\
\ar{إ} & \emph{alif with hamza below} & \textbf{\ar{إلى} \ar{اللقاء}} \emph{ilā l-liqāʾ} \\
\ar{ى} & \emph{alif maqṣūra} & \textbf{\ar{إلى} \ar{اللقاء}} \emph{ilā l-liqāʾ} \\
\ar{ف} & \emph{fāʾ} & \textbf{\ar{عفوا}} \emph{ʿafwan} \\
\ar{ق} & \emph{qāf} & \textbf{\ar{إلى} \ar{اللقاء}} \emph{ilā l-liqāʾ} \\
\ar{ض} & \emph{ḍād} & \textbf{\ar{من} \ar{فضلك}} \emph{min faḍlik} \\
\ar{آ} & \emph{alif madda} & \textbf{\ar{آسف}} \emph{āsif} \\
\ar{ز} & \emph{zāy} & \textbf{\ar{أزرق}} \emph{azraq} \\
\ar{غ} & \emph{ghayn} & \textbf{\ar{إلى} \ar{الغد}} \emph{ilā l-ghad} \\
\ar{ط} & \emph{ṭāʾ} & \textbf{\ar{طعام}} \emph{ṭaʿām} \\
\ar{ظ} & \emph{ẓāʾ} & \textbf{\ar{الظهر}} \emph{aẓ-ẓuhr} \\
\ar{ذ} & \emph{dhāl} & \textbf{\ar{ذهب}} \emph{dhahaba} \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Write it:} each letter in the table from memory, then check it
  \item \emph{Say it:} the word each one came from
  \item \emph{Write it:} the four one-dot pairs side by side: \ar{د} \ar{ذ}, \ar{ر} \ar{ز}, \ar{ص} \ar{ض}, \ar{ط} \ar{ظ}
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Which letters here never join to the letter after them? (\textbf{\ar{د} \ar{ذ} \ar{ز}}, and the alifs \textbf{\ar{إ} \ar{آ}}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
